study_name.evidence_quote: The Prevotella copri Complex Comprises Four Distinct Clades
study_name.notes: Study name derived from paper title and first author with year of publication.

target_condition.evidence_quote: P. copri is a common human gut microbe that has been both positively and negatively associated with host health. ten datasets including colorectal cancer (CRC), type 2 diabetes (T2D), hypertension, liver cirrhosis, and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)
target_condition.notes: Multiple conditions investigated in the meta-analysis of metagenomes.

zigosity.notes: No twin zygosity information reported in the paper.

age_min.notes: Paper reports age ranges for cohorts (e.g., Ghana: 20-45 yrs adults, 0-15 yrs children; Ethiopia: 22-45 yrs adults, 0.167-4.5 yrs infants; Tanzania: 18-61 yrs adults, 0-18 yrs children) but no minimum age threshold for the overall study.

age_max.notes: Paper reports age ranges for individual cohorts but no overall study-level maximum age threshold.

age_years.notes: This is a meta-analysis of >6,500 metagenomes spanning multiple populations with varying ages; no single age_years applies at study level.

antibiotics_current_use.notes: No information on antibiotic use status reported.

bmi.section: Results — Associating P. copri Clades with Metagenomically Investigated Human Diseases
bmi.notes: Paper mentions analyzing BMI as a factor but does not report specific BMI values: 'Finally, we considered if the P. copri complex could be associated with other factors such as body mass index (BMI) or age (Table S1).'

dietary_restriction.notes: No formal dietary restriction data reported; paper discusses general diet patterns (fiber-rich vs. Western) but not participant-specific restrictions.

disease.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
disease.section: STAR Methods — Experimental Model and Subject Details
disease.notes: The newly sequenced cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) are all healthy. The meta-analysis includes disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, IBD, hypertension, liver cirrhosis) but those are analyzed at the dataset level, not as individual participant samples in this study's primary cohorts.

disease_details.notes: Newly sequenced participants were healthy; no disease details for primary cohorts.

disease_response_orr.notes: No treatment response or cancer outcome measures reported.

disease_response_pfs.notes: This is a microbiome study, not a clinical trial with progression-free survival outcomes.

disease_response_recist.notes: This study does not evaluate cancer treatment response by RECIST criteria.

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool samples collected but no specific stool phenotype measurements (consistency, frequency, etc.) reported.

fmt_id.notes: No fecal microbiota transplantation intervention reported.

fmt_role.notes: This is an observational metagenomic study, not an FMT intervention trial.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Birth weight not reported for the cohort.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Although the study includes infants and mother-infant pairs, no feeding method data reported.

obgyn_birth_control.notes: No oral contraceptive use data reported.

obgyn_lactating.notes: Although mothers are included in the Ethiopian cohort (mother-infant pairs), lactation status not reported.

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: No current pregnancy status reported for participants.

smoker.notes: No smoking status or history reported.

treatment.notes: No treatment or medication data reported for primary cohorts; study is observational.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: This is a microbiome study of healthy and non-healthy populations; no tumor staging reported.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: P. copri is 39.1% prevalent in healthy individuals from current metagenomic profiles
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified; prevalence percentages and functional gene categories extracted as biomarkers

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: clade A being the most prevalent (91.5% in non-Westernized versus 26.9% in Westernized)

value: >6,500 metagenomes analyzed from 36 datasets across 6 continents and 25 countries
1,023 P. copri genomes reconstructed (17 isolates, 1,006 metagenome-assembled genomes)
Four distinct clades (A, B, C, D) with >10% inter-clade genetic divergence
All clades confirmed by isolate sequencing
98 additional genomes from non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Madagascar)
Ancient metagenomes analyzed: Iceman (5,300 years old) and Mexican coprolites (1,300±100 BP)
P. copri clades diversified 3.5-2.5 million years ago (clades A, D, C) and 6.5 million years ago (clade B split)
Clade delineation pre-dates human migratory waves out of Africa (~90-194 ka)
No strong disease associations found in meta-analysis of CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, and IBD cohorts
Multi-generational dietary modifications associated with reduced P. copri prevalence in Westernized populations
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: analysis of 6,874 publicly available metagenomes from 36 individual datasets representing six continents and 25 different countries
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive metadata on study scope, scale, evolutionary history, and disease associations

host_species.evidence_quote: Prevotella copri is a frequent inhabitant of the human intestinal microbiome
host_species.notes: Human is the host species for all gut microbiome samples analyzed in this study
